analysis.one_liner: Power Grid Corporation (government-owned) builds and operates India's interstate electricity transmission network under a CERC-regulated, cost-plus-return tariff model.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (declared Nov 1, 2026) showed consolidated PAT up 8.4% YoY to Rs 3,866 crore on total income of Rs 12,055 crore (+3%), with management flagging a regulatory-asset adjustment that affects like-for-like comparability. An interim dividend of Rs 3/share was declared with the record date falling tomorrow, November 6, 2026. The board also approved selling its stake in subsidiary CTUIL to Grid-India and exiting three joint ventures, and completed merging 28 wholly-owned transmission subsidiaries into two - routine corporate tidying, not a governance flag.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a government-controlled monopoly that owns the high-voltage power lines connecting India's grid - it earns a regulated, pre-approved return on the assets it builds, so its cash flows are very predictable. The tension: management keeps raising its capex targets (Rs 37,000-40,000 crore for this year, and talk of even more after) to plug in new renewable energy capacity, but actual profit growth has stayed in the single digits and the stock has gone nowhere over the past year despite that. The growth story is in the pipeline of projects, not yet in the numbers.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT was Rs 3,866 crore (+8.4% YoY; standalone PAT Rs 3,819 crore), but H1 FY27 EBITDA grew only 1% to Rs 19,778 crore even as PAT rose 4% - the gap is partly a regulatory-asset adjustment management says distorts the comparison, so treat the PAT growth rate with caution. FY26 full-year PAT grew a modest 3% to Rs 15,928 crore. On capex, management raised FY27 guidance to Rs 37,000-40,000 crore and widened (not narrowed) its capitalisation guidance to Rs 25,000-30,000 crore, citing persistent land/right-of-way delays despite new compensation rules - its own words were that 'no projects are stalled,' but state-level adoption of the rules is slower than hoped.
analysis.performance_read: At Rs 260.45 the stock sits 24.1% below its September 2024 peak of Rs 343.24, within its 52-week range of Rs 244.65-319.41. Over 1 year it is roughly flat (-0.42%) against the Nifty's -4.25% and peer ADANIENSOL's +50% - though that peer's own 5-year return is -21.24%, so its one-year jump is a bounce off a weak base, not evidence the sector broadly re-rated. Over 3 and 5 years Power Grid has beaten the Nifty comfortably (+39.2% vs +25.8% over 3Y; +134.5% vs +35.2% over 5Y). The company carried out two bonus share issues (roughly 4:3 each) in 2021 and 2023; unlike a demerger, bonus shares don't strip value out of the price series, so these long-term returns are already on a comparable, adjusted basis and need no further correction.
analysis.valuation_read: P/E is about 15.9x and P/B about 2.5x, with ROE near 16.5% - not expensive for a profit-growing company, but ROE here is flattered by leverage (debt-to-equity ~1.47x), typical for an asset-heavy regulated utility. ROCE of 9.74% is the more honest measure of what the underlying asset base earns, and it is unremarkable - broadly in line with the regulated return the business is designed to deliver. The stock trading 24% below its 2024 peak reflects slowing single-digit profit growth and repeated misses on capitalisation guidance, not an obvious market mispricing of a fast grower.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is meant to be volume-led - more transmission assets commissioned means more regulated revenue - but execution has been the binding constraint, not demand. FY26 PAT grew just 3% and H1FY27 EBITDA grew only 1%, with capitalisation repeatedly falling short of guidance due to land and right-of-way delays. Management is now promising a bigger capex ramp (Rs 37,000-40,000 crore this year, 'much beyond' that in FY28-29) tied to HVDC links and renewable-energy integration, so the growth case currently rests on a pipeline that hasn't yet shown up in reported profit growth.
analysis.health_read: Business risk, not financial risk, is the thing to watch. As a regulated utility, cash collection is strong (receivable days reported at just 10.54, system availability 99.81%), and profit converts reliably into cash and into the roughly Rs 9/share trailing dividend (3.46% yield). The debt-to-equity ratio of ~1.47x looks high in isolation but is normal and by design for a utility that funds long-duration, tariff-backed assets with matched long-term debt. The real risk is operational: land acquisition and right-of-way delays that have pushed capitalisation below the company's own guidance more than once.
analysis.ownership_read: The promoter is the Government of India at 51.34%, unchanged this quarter - pledging is not a relevant concept for a sovereign promoter and none is reported. Foreign institutions hold roughly 24% and domestic institutions (including mutual funds at ~12.8%) around 21%, with public shareholders making up only 3-4%. No marquee individual investor appears on the register - this is an institutionally and state-owned stock, not one with a well-known name attached.
strengths: Near-monopoly transmission network with 99.81% system availability and just 10.54 days of receivables - collection risk is minimal
Consolidated PAT grew 8.4% YoY in Q2 FY27 to Rs 3,866 crore, with a trailing dividend of Rs 9/share giving a 3.46% yield
FY27 capex guidance raised to Rs 37,000-40,000 crore, with management flagging even higher spend in FY28-29 on HVDC and renewable-integration projects
Government of India holds 51.34% with zero pledging risk, backed by a stable CERC-regulated tariff framework
watchpoints: Capitalisation guidance for FY27 was widened, not narrowed, to Rs 25,000-30,000 crore - right-of-way and land-compensation delays keep pushing actual spend behind targets
H1 FY27 EBITDA grew only 1% to Rs 19,778 crore even as PAT grew 4%, and Q2 included a regulatory-asset adjustment management flagged as affecting comparability
Stock is 24.1% below its September 2024 peak and essentially flat over the past year, even as capex guidance keeps rising - the market hasn't yet rewarded the bigger pipeline
ROCE of 9.74% is well below ROE of 16.49%, showing shareholder returns depend on leverage (D/E ~1.47x) rather than the underlying regulated asset base earning outsized returns
analysis.one_thing: Whether FY27 capitalisation actually lands within the newly widened Rs 25,000-30,000 crore range, or misses again - that tells you whether the right-of-way bottleneck behind the stock's stalled re-rating is easing.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 results, capex/capitalisation guidance, dividend record date and shareholding figures were cross-checked across multiple independent sources (Tribune, Goodreturns, Investing.com earnings transcript, psuwatch, trendlyne). One search result showed a conflicting FII holding figure (11.27% vs 24.03%); the 24.03% figure was used as it reconciles with the promoter/DII/public totals, and the outlier was set aside. P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE and debt-to-equity were sourced from third-party aggregators (ticker.finology, incredmoney) rather than the company's own filing - treat as indicative and verify on Screener before publishing.
